clue.text: Bad luck with firm going at start of Derby?

indicators.note: the first piece is placed at the start of the second, so it comes first

parts.note: in horse racing, firm ground is described as hard going
Derby is an English cheese, so it stands for cheese by example (hence the question mark)

explanation.surface: A punter laments bad luck when the ground firmed up before the Derby horse race began.
explanation.walkthrough: The Derby looks like the horse race, which fits 'going'; here it is the cheese. HARD CHEESE is British slang for bad luck.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard cheese is a British idiom for tough luck, said with little sympathy.

clue.text: Eats hot dish of meat and potatoes

parts.note: to have a meal is to eat, so eats gives has
H is the usual abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone eats a hot plate of meat and potatoes.
explanation.definitionFit: A hash is a dish of chopped cooked meat fried up with potatoes.

clue.text: Physical collapse I encountered during marathon, perhaps

indicators.note: something encountered during an event sits in the middle of it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a marathon is an example of a run, as the 'perhaps' signals
taken as written

explanation.surface: A runner describes collapsing physically in the middle of a marathon.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruin can mean a broken-down physical state, as in being a wreck of one's former self.

clue.text: Chat nesting a short time in barn adapted for new use, perhaps

indicators.note: nesting means holding something snugly inside, so the second piece is placed within the first

parts.words: barn adapted for new use, perhaps
parts.note: a barn turned into a house is an example of a conversion
T is the abbreviation for time, made short

explanation.surface: Neighbours chat about a converted barn where someone has briefly settled.
explanation.definitionFit: A conversation is a talk between people, a synonym for a chat.

clue.text: Cream offering reduced energy with fewer calories

parts.note: energy reduced to its abbreviation is E
lite is the food-label spelling for a lower-calorie version

explanation.surface: A dairy product is advertised as giving less energy and fewer calories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cream' looks like the dairy product of the surface; it means the best of a group.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream of something is its best part, just as an elite is the best of a group.

clue.text: Trace up to the time of being captured by travelling Incas

indicators.note: something captured is held inside its captors, so one piece goes inside the other
travelling suggests movement, so the letters of the word beside it are moved around

parts.note: till means up to the time of, as in 'wait till Friday'

explanation.surface: Travelling Incas take a captive, leaving only a trace up to that time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captured' paints the Incas taking a prisoner; really it only says one word sits inside the scrambled tribe's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A scintilla is a tiny amount, a trace or the barest hint of something.

clue.text: One who became Falstaff's companion following a drink

parts.note: Prince Hal is the young drinking companion of Falstaff in Shakespeare's Henry IV plays
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean figure takes up with the drunken knight Falstaff after a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: A HALF is a British way of ordering half a pint of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordering a half in a British pub gets you half a pint of beer, a common drink.

clue.text: Greedy old upper class wallowing in caviar is corrupt

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled or altered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: U is the old label for upper-class usage, as in U and non-U
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A greedy old aristocrat wallows in caviar and is morally corrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wallowing in' is only a link: the old upper-class letters are thrown into the pool with the caviar before 'corrupt' scrambles everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Avaricious means having an excessive desire for wealth, which is greed.

clue.text: Writer was aware of restriction about pages with unspecified number

parts.note: to have felt something is to have been aware of it

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: a tie is a restriction or constraint
N stands for an unspecified number in mathematics

explanation.surface: A writer knew of a limit on how many pages could be used.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' sounds like an author but is the pen itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A felt-tip pen is an instrument for writing, so it is literally a writer.

clue.text: Trained in biology, perhaps, so keeping nice and fit working out

indicators.note: keeping means holding within, so the first piece surrounds the second

parts.note: sic is Latin for so or thus

indicators.note: working out suggests change, so the letters of the words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A scientist stays nice and fit by exercising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working out' looks like gym exercise, matching 'fit'; it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone trained in biology is scientific, biology being one example of a science.

clue.text: What takes just seconds for Jack and Jill to fill atop hill, finally?

definitions.text: What takes just seconds for Jack and Jill to fill atop hill, finally?

indicators.note: to fill means to go into the space between, so these letters sit inside the others
finally picks the last letter of each of the two words
just seconds picks only the second letter of each name

explanation.surface: The nursery-rhyme pair need only a moment to fill their container at the top of the hill.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme Jack and Jill go up the hill to fetch a pail of water; the whole clue is both definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyme's container is a pail, which is what the pair go up the hill to fill.

clue.text: State of health of the legal system

definitions.meaning: a person's physical make-up and general health
the body of fundamental laws and principles by which a state is governed

explanation.definitionFit: Constitution means both a person's physical condition and a nation's founding body of law.

clue.text: Concerning nice post, it's turned out to be one dealing with callers

parts.note: re means concerning or about

indicators.note: turned out means made into something different, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: only the word it is fodder; the 's is the verb is, a link

explanation.surface: Someone is pleased that a nice job has come up dealing with callers.
explanation.walkthrough: Only 'it' of 'it's' is fodder; the 's is the verb is, joining the anagram to 'turned out'.
explanation.definitionFit: A receptionist greets visitors and answers phone calls, so deals with callers.

clue.text: Like this grid? Second number heads cell at the top with R in residence

indicators.note: heads means goes in front of, so the earlier pieces come before what follows

parts.note: mo is short for a moment, a second

indicators.note: at the top picks the first letter of the word
in places the letter inside the word for a residence

parts.note: a home is a residence
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions about a cell numbering system in a building's top floor.
explanation.walkthrough: A crossword grid is black and white only, hence 'like this grid'.
explanation.definitionFit: Monochrome means in one colour or black and white, as a crossword grid is.

clue.text: Viper's thrown in to bring back a state of excitement

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the other word

parts.note: to fetch is to go and bring back

indicators.note: thrown means confused or flung about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the 's is the verb is, not a letter

explanation.surface: A snake is hurled in to retrieve something, causing alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Viper's' is 'Viper is': the snake's name alone is scrambled by 'thrown' and set inside the verb for bring back.
explanation.definitionFit: Fever pitch is an idiom for a state of intense excitement.

clue.text: Topless sweethearts' ball is a recipe for such excess?

indicators.note: topless means losing the top, so the first letter is removed

parts.note: sweethearts are lovers
a pill is a small ball, and slang for a ball in sport

explanation.surface: A risque remark about a romantic ball where things get out of hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Overspill is what spills over, a surplus or excess.

clue.text: Vamp I married is appearing in show

indicators.note: appearing in means going inside, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: to prove something is to show it
taken as written

explanation.surface: A seductive woman I married performs in a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vamp' looks like a seductive woman; in music to vamp is to make up an accompaniment on the spot.
explanation.definitionFit: To vamp in music is to play an improvised accompaniment, so to improvise.

clue.text: Try to economise with green director sequestering millions

indicators.note: sequestering means keeping apart inside, so the first piece holds the second

parts.note: a skip is the captain who directs play in bowls, played on a green

explanation.surface: An environmentally minded company director hides away millions to save money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' suggests environmental politics; here it is the bowling green, where a skip directs the team.
explanation.definitionFit: To skimp is to spend or use less than needed, trying to economise.

clue.text: Hidden? That doesn't begin to be this!

definitions.text: Hidden? That doesn't begin to be this!

indicators.note: not beginning means losing the first letter

parts.note: covert means hidden or secret

explanation.surface: A teasing riddle about something concealed becoming its opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is wordplay and definition: lose the start of the word for hidden and you get its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means open and plainly visible, the opposite of hidden.

clue.text: Pressure to introduce licence for bromide

indicators.note: to introduce is to come in front of, so the first piece precedes the second

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for pressure in physics
latitude is freedom or licence to act

explanation.surface: Pressure is put on to bring in a licence for a chemical sedative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bromide' looks like the sedative chemical; it also means a trite, comforting saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A bromide is a dull, trite remark meant to soothe, just as a platitude is.

clue.text: Knowing Dad, Ma's out to reform the big beast

parts.note: hip means knowing or in the know
pop is a familiar word for father

indicators.note: to reform is to reshape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of the word as printed, apostrophe aside
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hip father and mother set out to change a large animal's ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knowing' and 'Dad' look like a family scene; they are simply synonyms placed first.
explanation.definitionFit: The hippopotamus is a huge African mammal, a classic big beast.

clue.text: Financial backer local to Islington

definitions.meaning: an investor who funds a theatre show or start-up
a district and Underground station in Islington, north London, named after an old inn

explanation.definitionFit: An angel is an investor in a show, and the Angel is an area of Islington in London.

clue.text: Endless writer's block

indicators.note: endless means losing the end, so the last letter is removed

parts.note: Nevil Shute was an English novelist (A Town Like Alice); the 's is the verb is

explanation.surface: An author suffers from writer's block that never ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer's block' reads as a phrase but splits: the writer is Nevil Shute, and block is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To shut a road or door is to block it, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Architect held up by wings at small scale?

definitions.meaning: Sir Christopher ..., designer of St Paul's Cathedral in London

definitions.text: held up by wings at small scale?
definitions.meaning: a tiny creature kept aloft by its wings, a small bird

explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Wren was a famous architect, and a wren is a very small bird that flies on little wings.

clue.text: Reluctant to throw out the first swear word

indicators.note: throwing out the first means removing the opening letter

parts.note: loath means reluctant or unwilling

explanation.surface: Someone is reluctant to be the first to utter a swear word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swear word' looks like a profanity; it is a solemn promise.
explanation.definitionFit: An oath is a solemn word sworn as a promise, so literally a swear word.

clue.text: Queen's husband, number three in RAF, is her flyer in blue

parts.note: a queen's husband in a royal pair of cards or chess might be the king

indicators.note: number three in picks the third letter of the word that follows

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A royal consort and an RAF officer admire a woman pilot in blue uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAF uniform is blue, so 'flyer in blue' suggests a pilot; it is the bright blue bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The kingfisher is a small bird with vivid blue plumage, a flyer in blue.

clue.text: Be suggestive of a group of screech owls

indicators.note: group of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A noisy parliament of owls seems to hint at something.
explanation.definitionFit: To echo something is to recall or be suggestive of it, as a style echoes an earlier one.

clue.text: Footwear very much in the forefront of graceful fashion

parts.note: well can mean very much, as in well pleased
taken as written

indicators.note: the forefront picks the first letter of the word

parts.note: ton is an old word for fashion, as in high society's 'the ton'

explanation.surface: Elegant footwear is very much leading the way in fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: A WELLINGTON is a British rubber boot, hardly graceful fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: A wellington is a waterproof rubber boot, a kind of footwear.
